bib.title: Patch n' Pack: NaViT, a Vision Transformer for any Aspect Ratio and Resolution

read.skipped: reference list skimmed only for lineage

question: Can Vision Transformers be trained on images at native aspect ratio and mixed resolution by packing patches from several images into one sequence, and does this improve training efficiency and flexibility?
hypothesis: Sequence packing, as used in NLP, lets ViTs process variable-resolution inputs with fixed batch shapes, giving more images per compute budget and better performance than fixed-resolution ViT.
contributions: Randomly sampling resolutions at training time significantly reduces training cost.
NaViT performs well across a wide range of resolutions, giving a smooth cost-performance trade-off at inference, and adapts to new tasks at lower cost.
Fixed batch shapes from example packing enable aspect-ratio-preserving resolution sampling, variable token dropping rates and adaptive computation.

method.summary: NaViT packs patches from multiple images into one fixed-length sequence (Patch n' Pack), with per-example attention and pooling masks, factorized/fractional positional embeddings, continuous token dropping and mixed-resolution sampling. It is pre-trained on JFT-4B (classification) and WebLI (contrastive) and compared with compute-matched ViTs, then transferred to classification, segmentation, detection and video.

training.objective: sigmoid cross-entropy classification on JFT-4B; contrastive image-text loss (chunked contrastive loss) on WebLI

limits: No code or weights release is mentioned; Emax, optimizer, warmup length, precision, seeds and parameter counts are not stated.
Pretraining sets JFT-4B and WebLI are proprietary; the Appendix A.1 learning-rate sentence is garbled in the PDF text.
Native-resolution training is not used by default; resolution is sampled to control throughput and packing.
Kinetics400 version used has less data than prior work, so the video comparison is weak.
OOD gains depend on preprocessing: central-crop ViT baseline favours ObjectNet, so differences vary by crop strategy.
Model-vs-human: ViT is mostly better than NaViT at higher fine-tune resolutions.
Authors caution that fairness-attribute classifiers can misidentify people and should be used only for auditing or dataset diversity measurement.
NaViT does not build hierarchical multi-scale representations; combining the two is left as future work.
Single runs; no variance or seeds reported except the Wilcoxon tests on fairness probes.

terms.definition: Multiple patches from different images are packed in a single sequence, which enables variable resolution while preserving the aspect ratio.
Native Resolution ViT, a ViT trained with sequence packing on images at their native resolution and aspect ratio.
Images with the same area as a square image with a given resolution.
The token dropping rate can be varied per-image rather than being the same proportion for all examples.
